newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr at 95-105 yen appropriate - US auto group chief.
newsitem.headline: Dlr at 95-105 yen appropriate - US auto group chief.

text.p: Japanese fundamentals suggest that a dollar exchange rate of 95-105 yen is an appropriate level, Andrew Card, president of the American Automobile Manufacturers' Association, said on Thursday.

"My personal view is that the yen should trade in the 95-105 yen to a dollar range. That's what the fundamentals of the Japanese economy should suggest with a move toward deregulation," Card told Reuters Financial Television.
He said he was pleased that the yen has strengthened from its recent low of over 127 yen to a dollar, but added that he saw room for it to rise more.
Card said that the recent big surge in Japanese auto exports to the United States was a result of the excessively weak yen.
U.S. auto makers have seen market share shift to the Japanese because the weaker yen has given the Japanese greater flexibility in pricing and marketing, he added.
Meanwhile, progress in opening up more U.S. dealerships in Japan has been 'pitiful', he said.

There were modest expectations that after the U.S.-Japan car agreement of August 1995 the U.S. auto makers could have 200 high-volume vehicle outlets in Japan by the end of this year. But they have only 126 outlets, he added.

He said he hoped that the Japanese government can stimulate more consumer demand because the consumption tax increase to five percent from three in April has had a dampening effect on the demand, in particular, on imports.
"The U.S. administration understands that the growing trade surplus in Japan has the potential of increasing trade friction with Japan," Card said.
The U.S. Trade Representatives office and the Department of Commerce will continue to monitor what is happening in the market, he said.
The two-year anniversary of the 1995 U.S.-Japan auto pact is soon, and a U.S. government review of the pact is likely to show that progress has been disappointing, he added.
